title: Space Tech Briefing — October 06, 2026
summary:
Good morning, future voyagers and space fanatics! It's Tuesday, October 06, 2026, and the cosmos is absolutely buzzing with activity. I'm your host, ready to launch you into the latest and greatest from the world of space technology!

First up, we have some exciting news for European space fans! ESA's very own French astronaut, Sophie Adenot, and her three incredible Crew-12 teammates are preparing to bid farewell to the International Space Station! Their mission is wrapping up, with the crew set to depart the orbiting laboratory tomorrow, Wednesday, October 7th, at 2:05 PM French time. We're expecting their triumphant return to Earth on Thursday, October 8th. What an incredible journey for Sophie and the entire Crew-12 team! We'll be tracking their progress closely.

Now, as we await these upcoming returns, let's cast our minds back to a major story that's still unfolding in the world of commercial spaceflight. As a highlight of recent space developments, NASA and Boeing announced back on September 28th that the Starliner spacecraft is slated for another uncrewed flight. This crucial mission is expected to take place by the end of this year or early 2027. This comes after the Starliner, the second vessel in NASA's Commercial Crew program designed to ferry astronauts to the ISS, faced significant challenges. You might recall the first crewed flight, CFT-1, in 2024, which encountered numerous technical failures. Those issues led to the Starliner returning to Earth *without* its crew, leaving astronauts Sunita Williams and Butch Willmore on the ISS for a prolonged stay of 286 days, far beyond the initial 8 to 10 days planned. An independent review committee identified three major problems, notably classifying propulsion failures as a "near-miss accident" that put the astronauts in danger. So, this upcoming uncrewed flight is a critical step for Starliner as it aims to prove its readiness for future human missions.

And that's your morning briefing from the edge of the atmosphere and beyond! Thank you for tuning in, and remember to keep looking up! Have a stellar day, everyone.
